questions.question: Who became the Chairperson of ISRO in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. V Narayanan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **January 2025**, the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)** approved the appointment of **Dr. V Narayanan** as the new **Chairperson** of the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.
 
• Alongside the role of **ISRO Chairperson**, he also assumed the charges of **Secretary**, **Department of Space (DoS)**, and **Chairman** of the **Space Commission**.
 
• **Dr. V Narayanan** succeeded **S. Somanath**, whose distinguished three-year tenure concluded in **January 2025**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Dr. V Narayanan.***
 
• Prior to his appointment as the head of the Indian space agency, **Dr. Narayanan** served as the **Director** of the **Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC)**, a key unit of **ISRO** located in **Valiamala**, **Thiruvananthapuram**.
 
• He is widely recognized as a leading expert in **Cryogenic Propulsion Technology** and played a critical role in the development of the **CE-20 engine**, which powers the **LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-III)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO):**
 
 
• **ISRO** was established on **August 15, 1969**, superseding the Indian National Committee for Space Research (**INCOSPAR**).
 
• The organization is headquartered in **Bengaluru**, **Karnataka**, and functions under the **Department of Space**, which reports directly to the **Prime Minister of India**.
 
• The first Chairman of **ISRO** was **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai**, who is considered the **Father of the Indian Space Program**.
 
 
 
• **Department of Space (DoS) and Space Commission:**
 
 
• The **Department of Space** and the **Space Commission** were established by the **Government of India** in **1972** to promote the development and application of space science and technology.
 
• The **Chairman** of **ISRO** traditionally holds the ex-officio position of **Secretary (DoS)** to ensure seamless administrative and technical coordination.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Overview:**
 
 
• **S. Somanath:** Served as the **10th Chairman** of **ISRO** from **January 2022** to **January 2025**. His tenure saw the historic success of **Chandrayaan-3** and the launch of **Aditya-L1**.
 
• **K. Radhakrishnan:** He was the **Chairman** of **ISRO** from **2009** to **2014**, leading the successful **Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan)**.
 
• **A. Sivathanu Pillai:** A renowned scientist known as the **Father of BrahMos**, he served as the **CEO** and **Managing Director** of **BrahMos Aerospace** and was a former Chief Controller of **DRDO**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dr. V Narayanan** joined **ISRO** in **1984** and has contributed significantly to the Indian space program for over **40 years**.
 
• He has been instrumental in the **Chandrayaan-2** and **Chandrayaan-3** missions, specifically overseeing the propulsion systems required for complex lunar landings.
 
• Under his leadership, **ISRO** is expected to prioritize upcoming ambitious projects such as the **Gaganyaan** (India's first human spaceflight mission), the **Bhartiya Antariksh Station**, and the **Shukrayaan** (Venus orbiter) mission.
 
• He has received numerous accolades, including the **ISRO Performance Excellence Award** and the **Team Excellence Award** for his contributions to rocket propulsion.
</ul

questions.question: In June 2025, which companies received the technology for the 70-ton Tank Transporter Trailer for MBT Arjun Mk-1A?

options.text: Metaltech Motor Bodies Pvt Ltd, Goma Engineering Pvt Ltd, John Galt International
BEML Ltd, Tata International Vehicle Applications, SDR Auto Pvt Ltd, John Galt International
Bharat Electronics Ltd, Tata Advanced Systems Ltd, John Galt International
Bharat Forge, Dass Hitachi Ltd, John Galt International

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**BEML Ltd, Tata International Vehicle Applications, SDR Auto Pvt Ltd, John Galt International**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **June 2025**, the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** reached a significant milestone in defense indigenization by transferring the technology for the **70-ton Tank Transporter Trailer**.
 
• The **Combat Vehicles Research and Development Establishment (CVRDE)**, a premier lab of DRDO based in **Avadi**, handed over the **Transfer of Technology (ToT)** documents to four major industry partners.
 
• The recipient companies include **BEML Ltd**, **Tata International Vehicle Applications (TIVA)**, **SDR Auto Pvt Ltd**, and **John Galt International**. ***Hence, the correct answer is BEML Ltd, Tata International Vehicle Applications, SDR Auto Pvt Ltd, John Galt International.***
 
• This **70-ton trailer** has been specifically designed and developed to meet the logistical requirements of transporting the **Main Battle Tank (MBT) Arjun Mk-1A**, which is the heaviest tank in the **Indian Army's** inventory.
 
• The move aims to boost **domestic manufacturing** capabilities and ensure that multiple production lines are available to meet the induction timelines of the armored regiments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **MBT Arjun Mk-1A:**
 
 
• The **Arjun Mk-1A** is an upgraded variant of the **Arjun Mark-1** tank, featuring **71 new upgrades** compared to the earlier version.
 
• It weighs approximately **68.5 tonnes**, making it one of the heaviest main battle tanks in the world, necessitating specialized **70-ton capacity trailers** for road mobility.
 
• The tank features enhanced **firepower**, a **Superior Transmission System**, and indigenous **Explosive Reactive Armour (ERA)**.
 
 
 
• **Industry Partners:**
 
 
• **BEML Ltd**: A **Schedule 'A' Company** under the **Ministry of Defence**, it plays a pivotal role in serving India's core sectors like Defence, Rail, Power, and Mining.
 
• **Tata International Vehicle Applications (TIVA)**: A leading player in the **trailer manufacturing** industry, providing specialized transport solutions for heavy equipment.
 
• **John Galt International** and **SDR Auto**: These firms represent the growing participation of the **private sector** in the **Indian Defence** supply chain under the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative.
 
 
 
• **CVRDE (Combat Vehicles Research and Development Establishment):**
 
 
• Located in **Chennai**, this laboratory is responsible for the design and development of **armoured fighting vehicles** and tracked components.
 
• It successfully integrated the **70-ton transporter** project to ensure the **MBT Arjun** can be deployed rapidly across different sectors using the **National Highway** network.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Logistics and Mobility:** The **70-ton Tank Transporter Trailer** is a **multi-axle** vehicle system designed to operate in various terrains, ensuring the **MBT Arjun Mk-1A** can be moved from peace stations to forward areas efficiently.
 
• **Indigenous Development:** The project emphasizes the **Make in India** philosophy, reducing the reliance on imported heavy-haulage equipment for the **Ministry of Defence**.
 
• **Technical Specs:** The trailer is equipped with advanced **hydraulic systems** and high-strength steel to withstand the immense weight and pressure of the **68.5-ton tank** during long-distance transit.
 
• **Year of Milestone:** The formal handover of technology in **June 2025** marks a critical step toward the full operationalization of the new **Arjun** regiments ordered by the **Indian Army**.
</ul

questions.question: As per the Transparency International report released in February 2025, what was India’s rank in the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**96**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Transparency International** released the **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) 2024** in **February 2025**, providing a global snapshot of public sector corruption.
 
• In the **2024** rankings, **India** was placed at the **96th** position among **180 countries** and territories.
 
• India’s overall score in **2024** was **39** on a scale where **0** is "highly corrupt" and **100** is "very clean."
 
• Compared to the previous year's report (**CPI 2023**), where India held the **93rd** rank, the country has seen a slight decline in its standing by three positions.
 
• The report highlights that India’s score has shown fluctuations but remains below the global average, reflecting ongoing challenges in curbing **public sector corruption** and ensuring **transparency**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 96**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Transparency International:**
 
 
• It is an international **non-governmental organization** founded in **1993**.
 
• The organization is headquartered in **Berlin, Germany**, and operates in more than **100 countries**.
 
• It is primarily known for the **Corruption Perceptions Index**, the **Global Corruption Barometer**, and the **Bribe Payers Index**.
 
 
 
• **Scoring and Ranking Mechanism:**
 
 
• The **CPI** uses **13** different data sources from **12** independent institutions to aggregate perceptions of corruption.
 
• These institutions include the **World Bank**, the **World Economic Forum**, and the **Economist Intelligence Unit**.
 
• A country's rank indicates its position relative to other countries in the index, while its **score** indicates the perceived level of corruption.
 
 
 
• **Global Performance in 2024:**
 
 
• **Denmark** topped the index once again with a score of **90**, followed by **Finland** and **New Zealand**.
 
• At the opposite end of the spectrum, **Somalia**, **Syria**, and **South Sudan** were ranked at the bottom of the list.
 
• The **global average score** for the **2024** index remained stagnant at **43**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **South Asian Comparison:**
 
 
• Among its neighbors, **Bhutan** continues to perform exceptionally well, ranking **26th** with a score of **68**.
 
• **Pakistan** was ranked lower at **133rd**, while **Bangladesh** was positioned at **149th** in the **2024** report.
 
• **India** shares the **96th** rank with countries like the **Maldives**.
 
 
 
• **Implications for India:**
 
 
• The **96th rank** suggests a need for stronger **anti-corruption laws**, better **whistleblower protection**, and enhanced **institutional independence**.
 
• Corruption levels often impact **foreign direct investment (FDI)** and the overall **ease of doing business** in a nation.
 
• The **2024 report** emphasizes that countries with weak **justice systems** tend to struggle more with systemic corruption.
 
 

4d

questions.question: What has the Supreme Court made mandatory for judicial service applicants in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three years of legal practice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India** has reiterated the importance of practical experience for those entering the judiciary, making **three years of legal practice** as an advocate a mandatory criterion for judicial service applicants.
 
• This mandate is set to be strictly enforced for recruitment cycles and examinations scheduled for **May 2025** and onwards, ensuring that candidates possess foundational courtroom exposure.
 
• The decision aims to address the lack of practical knowledge often seen in fresh law graduates who previously could appear for the **Civil Judge (Junior Division)** exams immediately after their degree.
 
• By requiring a minimum of **3 years** of practice, the judiciary intends to ensure that new officers are well-versed in procedural laws, **Trial Court** etiquette, and the nuances of litigation.
 
• The **Bar Council of India (BCI)** has been a strong proponent of this requirement, arguing that the maturity gained through **legal practice** is essential for the responsibilities of a judicial officer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Legal Framework:** The recruitment of the subordinate judiciary in India is governed by **Article 234** of the **Constitution of India**, which involves the **State Public Service Commission** and the respective **High Court**.
 
• **Historical Context:** In the **2002** judgment of the **All India Judges Association v. Union of India**, the **Supreme Court** had previously allowed fresh law graduates to sit for exams, but recent discussions have shifted back toward the **three-year experience** rule to improve judicial quality.
 
• **Role of the BCI:** The **Bar Council of India**, established under the **Advocates Act, 1961**, regulates legal education and professional conduct, and it has consistently advocated for mandatory practice to maintain the standards of the **legal profession**.
 
• **Implementation:** Several states, including **Andhra Pradesh**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and **Gujarat**, had already moved towards incorporating this **three-year** experience requirement into their **Judicial Service Rules** prior to the broader national emphasis.
 
• **Training Benefits:** Mandatory practice reduces the extensive hand-holding required during the initial training phase at **State Judicial Academies**, as candidates already understand the basic filing and hearing processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility Age:** While the practice requirement has changed, the typical age limit for the **Lower Judicial Service** remains between **21 and 35 years** for general category candidates, with relaxations for reserved categories.
 
• **Higher Judicial Service (HJS):** It is important to distinguish this from the **Higher Judicial Service**, which requires a minimum of **7 years of practice** as an advocate for direct recruitment as a **District Judge** under **Article 233**.
 
• **Law Degree Requirement:** Regardless of the practice mandate, an applicant must hold a **Bachelor of Laws (LL.B)** degree from a university recognized by the **Bar Council of India**.
 
• **Examination Structure:** The **Judicial Service Examination** typically consists of three stages: the **Preliminary Examination** (objective), the **Main Examination** (descriptive), and the **Viva-Voce** (interview).
</ul

questions.question: The Ministry of Heavy Industries, Government of India, introduced a programme in July 2025 to give financial support for electric trucks under ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PM E-DRIVE initiative**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **PM E-DRIVE** (Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement) scheme was approved by the Union Cabinet to promote **electric mobility** in India, succeeding the **FAME-II** program.
 
• The initiative is administered by the **Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI)** and focuses on providing **financial incentives** for the purchase of various categories of electric vehicles.
 
• Specifically, for the first time, the government has allocated **Rs 500 crore** dedicated to providing incentives for **electric trucks** (e-trucks) to promote decarbonization in the logistics and freight sector. ***Hence, the correct answer is PM E-DRIVE initiative.***
 
• The primary goal of including **electric trucks** is to reduce the environmental impact of heavy-duty vehicles, which are significant contributors to **CO2 emissions** and air pollution in the country.
 
• Under this initiative, the government provides support to buyers of **e-trucks** that possess a **scrapage certificate** from an authorized **Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facility (RVSF)**, encouraging the removal of older, polluting commercial vehicles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Financial Outlay:** The **PM E-DRIVE** scheme has a total budgetary outlay of **Rs 10,900 crore** over a period of **two years** (spanning **2024-25** and **2025-26**).
 
• **E-Voucher System:** To simplify the process of claiming subsidies, the **Ministry of Heavy Industries** introduced **Aadhaar-authenticated e-vouchers**. These are generated at the time of purchase and are essential for the **Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs)** to claim reimbursement.
 
• **Broad Vehicle Coverage:** Besides e-trucks, the scheme supports **24.79 lakh e-2Ws**, **3.16 lakh e-3Ws**, and **14,028 e-buses**, ensuring a holistic transition toward green transport.
 
• **Charging Infrastructure:** A significant portion of the fund, **Rs 2,000 crore**, is earmarked for the installation of **Electric Vehicle Public Charging Stations (EVPCS)** in high-traffic cities and on major highways to tackle range anxiety.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Incentive for E-Ambulances:** The **PM E-DRIVE** scheme also marks the first time the government is providing **Rs 500 crore** specifically for **e-ambulances** to encourage eco-friendly emergency medical services.
 
• **Phased Manufacturing Programme (PMP):** To boost the **Make in India** initiative, the scheme enforces **PMP** guidelines, ensuring that a significant percentage of **EV components** are manufactured domestically to strengthen the local supply chain.
 
• **Modernization of Testing Agencies:** The **Ministry of Heavy Industries** has also allocated **Rs 780 crore** for the **upgradation** and modernization of testing agencies to handle the emerging **green technologies** and ensure safety standards.
 
• **Impact on Environment:** By targeting high-mileage segments like trucks and buses, the scheme aims to achieve a substantial reduction in **fossil fuel consumption** and meet India's **Net Zero** targets by **2070**.
</ul

questions.question: According to the Sustainable Development Goals National Indicator Framework progress report, 2025, published in June 2025, the number of waste recycling plants in India increased from 829 in 2019–20 to 3,036 in 2024–25. This improvement primarily contributes to which Sustainable Development Goal (SDG)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SDG 12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goal 12 (SDG 12)** is titled "**Responsible Consumption and Production**," which aims to ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns.
 
• According to the **Sustainable Development Goals National Indicator Framework (NIF)** progress report **2025**, the number of waste recycling plants in India saw a significant surge, rising from **829 in the year 2019–20** to **3,036 in the year 2024–25**.
 
• This expansion directly supports **SDG Target 12.5**, which mandates that by **2030**, nations should substantially reduce waste generation through **prevention, reduction, recycling, and reuse**.
 
• The **National Indicator Framework (NIF)** was developed by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** to track India's journey toward achieving the **Global SDGs**.
 
• The growth in recycling infrastructure reflects India's transition toward a **Circular Economy**, where resources are kept in use for as long as possible. ***Hence, the mention of waste recycling plants aligns perfectly with SDG 12.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production):**
 
 
• It encompasses **11 targets**, including the **sustainable management** of natural resources, reducing **food waste**, and encouraging companies to adopt sustainable practices.
 
• In the context of **India**, initiatives like **Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR)** for plastic and e-waste are critical drivers for this goal.
 
 
 
• **SDG 2 (Zero Hunger):**
 
 
• This goal focuses on ending hunger, achieving **food security**, improving **nutrition**, and promoting **sustainable agriculture** by the year **2030**.
 
 
 
• **SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation):**
 
 
• It ensures the availability and **sustainable management of water** and sanitation for all, including targets for **water quality** and **wastewater treatment**.
 
 
 
• **SDG 15 (Life on Land):**
 
 
• This goal is dedicated to protecting, restoring, and promoting the sustainable use of **terrestrial ecosystems**, managing **forests**, and halting **biodiversity loss**.
 
 
 
• **The 2030 Agenda:**
 
 
• Adopted by **193 UN Member States** in **September 2015**, the agenda consists of **17 Sustainable Development Goals** and **169 targets** designed to be a "blueprint to achieve a better and more sustainable future for all."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **NITI Aayog** is the nodal agency in India for coordinating and monitoring the **SDGs** at the national and sub-national levels through the **SDG India Index**.
 
• The **MoSPI** publishes the **National Indicator Framework (NIF)** reports annually to provide a data-driven perspective on progress across different sectors like **health, education, and environment**.
 
• The sharp increase in recycling plants between **2019 and 2025** highlights the impact of the **Swachh Bharat Mission 2.0**, which emphasizes **zero waste** and scientific processing of municipal solid waste.

7f

questions.question: What is the percentage of the Contingent Risk Buffer set by the Reserve Bank of India in May 2025 for FY 2024–25?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7.5%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Central Board of Directors** of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, during its meeting held in **May 2025**, decided to increase the **Contingent Risk Buffer (CRB)** to **7.5%** for the **Financial Year 2024-25**.
 
• This decision was made while approving the transfer of **surplus** to the **Central Government** for the accounting year ended **March 31, 2025**.
 
• The **CRB** is a specific fund maintained by the **RBI** to cover **unforeseen contingencies** arising from **monetary** and **financial stability** operations, **systemic risks**, and **operational risks**.
 
• For the previous financial year (**FY 2023-24**), the **RBI** had maintained the **CRB** at **6.5%**, but the increase to **7.5%** in **2025** reflects a cautious approach to maintaining a robust **balance sheet** amidst evolving global economic conditions.
 
• The **RBI** follows the **Economic Capital Framework (ECF)** to determine the appropriate level of **risk buffers** and the amount of **dividend** to be paid to the **Government of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Economic Capital Framework (ECF):** 
 
 
• The framework was reviewed by the **Bimal Jalan Committee**, which submitted its report in **August 2019**.
 
• The committee recommended that the **Contingent Risk Buffer** should be maintained within a range of **5.5% to 6.5%** of the **RBI's balance sheet**.
 
• However, the **RBI Board** has the authority to adjust this percentage based on **macroeconomic stability** and **financial risk** assessments, as seen in the **May 2025** decision to raise it to **7.5%**.
 
 
 
• **Surplus Distribution Policy:**
 
 
• The **RBI** earns income through **interest on government securities**, **foreign exchange interventions**, and **liquidity adjustment facilities**.
 
• After deducting **operating expenses** and **provisions** for **contingency funds**, the remaining **surplus** is transferred to the **Union Government** under **Section 47** of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• This transfer serves as a non-tax revenue source for the **Government of India**, helping to manage the **fiscal deficit**.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Central Board:**
 
 
• The **RBI's** affairs are governed by the **Central Board of Directors**, which is appointed by the **Government of India**.
 
• The **Governor** and **Deputy Governors** are part of this board, which oversees the **monetary policy** and **financial health** of the **central bank**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: Which institute partnered with NDMA in 2025 to develop tunnel safety guidelines?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IIT Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2025**, the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** officially partnered with the **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi** to formulate specialized **tunnel safety guidelines**.
 
• The primary objective of this collaboration is to establish a robust framework for the **design, construction, and operation** of tunnels across India, particularly in ecologically sensitive and geologically challenging regions like the **Himalayas**. ***Hence, the option IIT Delhi is correct.***
 
• The partnership focuses on creating **Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)** that incorporate advanced **geotechnical monitoring** and **structural health assessment** tools to prevent collapses and accidents.
 
• **IIT Delhi** was chosen due to its extensive research capabilities in **Civil Engineering** and **Underground Space Technology**, providing the necessary technical expertise to the **NDMA**.
 
• These guidelines are intended to serve as a mandatory reference for all infrastructure agencies, ensuring that **safety audits** and **emergency evacuation protocols** are integrated from the project's inception.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA):**
 
 
• It is the apex statutory body for disaster management in **India**, established under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**.
 
• The **Prime Minister of India** serves as the ex-officio **Chairperson** of the **NDMA**.
 
• Its mandate includes laying down policies, plans, and guidelines for disaster management to ensure a timely and effective response to **natural and man-made disasters**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Tunnel Safety in India:**
 
 
• With the expansion of the **Char Dham Project** and various strategic **railway tunnels** in **Jammu & Kashmir** and **Arunachal Pradesh**, tunnel safety has become a national priority.
 
• The **2023 Silkyara tunnel collapse** in **Uttarakhand**, where **41 workers** were trapped for 17 days, served as a major catalyst for the **2025** initiative to formalize safety standards.
 
• Key safety features now emphasized include **escape passages**, **automated ventilation systems**, **fire suppressants**, and **real-time sensor-based monitoring**.
 
 
 
• **Role of IIT Delhi:**
 
 
• As an **Institute of Eminence (IoE)**, **IIT Delhi** leads several national-level research projects in **disaster-resilient infrastructure**.
 
• The institute's **Department of Civil Engineering** provides consultancy for high-altitude construction, focusing on **rock mechanics** and **seismic stability**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographical Context:** Most tunnel projects in India are located in the **Young Fold Mountains** (Himalayas), which are prone to **landslides**, **seismic activity**, and **fragile rock formations**.
 
• **Policy Integration:** The guidelines developed by **IIT Delhi** and **NDMA** are expected to be adopted by the **Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH)** and the **National Highways and Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (NHIDCL)**.
 
• **Technological Deployment:** Future tunnels will likely see the mandatory installation of **SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition)** systems for centralized safety management as per the new **2025** recommendations.
</ul

• The **IGU** is affiliated with the **International Golf Federation** and play a vital role in selecting the **Indian national team** for international events like the **Asian Games** and **Olympics**.

• **Significance of the Title**: Winning an **IGU major** is a prerequisite for climbing the **National Order of Merit**. High rankings in this system allow young golfers to represent **India** at prestigious international amateur tournaments.
 
• **Other Options**:
 
 
• **Shubhankar Sharma** and **Gaganjeet Bhullar** are established **professional golfers** who have already won multiple international titles on the **European** and **Asian Tours**.
 
• **Shiv Kapur** is an **Asian Games gold medalist** and a veteran of the professional circuit, distinguishably different from the junior category winners.

questions.question: In November 2025, India conducted the bilateral military exercise ‘AJEYA WARRIOR-25’ with which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United Kingdom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The bilateral military exercise **AJEYA WARRIOR-25** is a joint training initiative conducted between the **Indian Army** and the **British Army** of the **United Kingdom**.
 
• The **2025 edition** marks the **8th edition** of this biennial training event, aimed at strengthening **military-to-military cooperation** and fostering **bilateral relations** between the two nations.
 
• The primary objective of this exercise is to build **positive military relations**, enhance **interoperability**, and share **best practices** while undertaking **company-level operations** in **urban and semi-urban terrain**.
 
• During **AJEYA WARRIOR**, troops from both countries engage in various tactical drills, including **counter-insurgency** and **counter-terrorism** operations under a **United Nations mandate**.
 
• The exercise typically involves the participation of infantry regiments; for instance, the **Indian Army** is often represented by a battalion of the **Gorkha Rifles**, while the **British Army** contributes soldiers from various units like the **Royal Gurkha Rifles** or the **1st Battalion Merician Regiment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Defense Cooperation with the UK**: 
 
 
• Apart from the army exercise, **India** and the **United Kingdom** conduct high-level exercises across all three services. **Exercise KONKAN** is the bilateral **naval exercise** between the **Indian Navy** and the **Royal Navy**.
 
• **Exercise Indradhanush** is the joint **air force exercise** involving the **Indian Air Force (IAF)** and the **Royal Air Force (RAF)** of the **UK**.
 
• The defense relationship is guided by the **2030 Roadmap**, which was agreed upon in **May 2021** to elevate the bilateral tie to a **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Exercise**:
 
 
• The **AJEYA WARRIOR** series started in **2005**. It alternates between **India** (often at **Chaubatia, Uttarakhand**) and the **United Kingdom** (often at **Salisbury Plains**).
 
• It provides a platform for **Combat Conditioning**, **Tactical Training**, and **Joint Command Post** exercises, ensuring that both forces are prepared for modern-day security challenges.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Partnership**: The **United Kingdom** is a key defense partner for India in Western Europe, collaborating on **maritime domain awareness**, **cyber security**, and **defense industrial production**.
 
• **Historical Context**: The previous edition, **AJEYA WARRIOR-23**, was held at **Salisbury Plains, UK** in **April-May 2023**, showcasing the **interoperability** of both armies in **simulated combat environments**.
 
• **Global Mandate**: Both nations emphasize that these exercises are not just bilateral but are designed to improve the **collective capability** of their forces to respond to **global security threats** and participate in **peacekeeping missions**.
</ul

questions.question: Who among the following received the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in 2025?

• She secured **bronze medals** in both the **women’s 10m air pistol** event and the **10m air pistol mixed team** event (alongside **Sarabjot Singh**).
 
• The **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** is the **highest sporting honor** in India, awarded annually by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**.
 
• The selection for the **2025** award recognizes her consistent excellence and her role in elevating the status of **shooting** in India on the global stage over the preceding four-year cycle.

• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award:**
 
 
• This award was instituted in the year **1991-92** and was previously known as the **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award**. It was renamed in **August 2021** in honor of the hockey legend **Major Dhyan Chand**.
 
• The award carries a **cash prize** of **Rs. 25 lakh**, a **certificate**, and a **medallion**.
 
• The first recipient of this prestigious award was the **Chess Grandmaster Vishwanathan Anand**.
 
 
 
• **Profile of Manu Bhaker:**
 
 
• She hails from the **Jhajjar** district of **Haryana**, India, and was born on **February 18, 2002**.
 
• Apart from her **Olympic** glory, she has won multiple gold medals at the **ISSF World Cup**, **Commonwealth Games**, and **Asian Games**.
 
• She represents the **younger generation** of Indian athletes who have dominated the **10m Air Pistol** category globally.

• The **National Sports Awards** are usually announced by the **Government of India** to recognize and reward excellence in sports.
 
• The **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna** is awarded for the most outstanding performance by a sportsperson over a period of **four years**.
 
• Other categories of National Sports Awards include the **Arjuna Award** (for consistent outstanding performance), the **Dronacharya Award** (for coaches), and the **Dhyan Chand Award** (for lifetime achievement).
 
• The **2025** awards highlight the continued dominance of **shooting** as a key sport where India achieves high-level **international success**.

questions.question: Which state launched new minority welfare schemes in September 2025, the Revanth Anna ka Sahara-Miskeen la Kosam, focusing on women empowerment and financial assistance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Telangana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The state of **Telangana**, under the leadership of Chief Minister **A. Revanth Reddy**, officially launched the **Revanth Anna ka Sahara-Miskeen la Kosam** scheme in **September 2025**.
 
• The scheme is a comprehensive welfare initiative designed specifically to provide **financial assistance** and **social security** to the **minority communities**, particularly focusing on those living below the poverty line.
 
• The title of the scheme, "**Revanth Anna ka Sahara**," translates to "Support from Brother Revanth," signifying the government's direct outreach to the **destitute (Miskeen)** and vulnerable sections of society.
 
• A primary pillar of this initiative is **women empowerment**, where financial grants and **skill development** opportunities are provided to minority women to encourage **entrepreneurship** and self-reliance.
 
• This move is part of the broader **Indiramma Rajyam** vision of the **Telangana Government**, aiming to ensure that the benefits of economic growth reach the last person in the **minority social hierarchy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Minority Welfare Framework in Telangana:**
 
 
• The **Minority Welfare Department** in **Telangana** is responsible for the implementation of policies for the socio-economic and educational development of **Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Jains, Buddhists, and Parsis**.
 
• The state has consistently allocated significant portions of its **annual budget** toward minority-specific schemes to improve the **literacy rate** and **employment** prospects within these communities.
 
 
 
• **Shaadi Mubarak Scheme:**
 
 
• This is another flagship initiative in **Telangana** that provides a **one-time financial grant** of approximately **Rs. 1,00,116** to the families of minority brides to alleviate the burden of **marriage expenses**.
 
• It serves as a counterpart to the **Kalyana Lakshmi Scheme**, which is available to other sections of the population.
 
 
 
• **Economic Support Schemes (ESS):**
 
 
• The **Telangana State Minorities Finance Corporation (TSMFC)** provides **subsidies** ranging from **50% to 80%** on bank-linked loans for **self-employment** projects.
 
• These loans are targeted at **unemployed youth** and small-scale vendors to help them establish **micro-enterprises**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Educational Empowerment:**
 
 
• The **Chief Minister’s Overseas Scholarship Scheme** provides financial assistance of up to **Rs. 20 lakhs** to meritorious minority students pursuing **Post Graduate** or **Ph.D.** studies in recognized foreign universities.
 
• Additionally, the state manages **Minority Residential Schools (TMREIS)**, which provide **high-quality English medium education**, free boarding, and lodging to thousands of students across **Telangana**.
 
 
 
• **Praja Palana Integration:**
 
 
• The **September 2025** schemes are integrated with the **Praja Palana** (People's Governance) mechanism, where applications are collected during **Gram Sabhas** to ensure transparency and eliminate middlemen.
 
• Eligibility is generally determined by the **Annual Income** of the family, which must be below a specific threshold (e.g., **Rs. 1.5 lakhs** in rural areas and **Rs. 2 lakhs** in urban areas).
